alternatives.concept: Study political power through comparative politics, international relations, European institutions and public policy. Political theory, law, history, economics and qualitative and quantitative research support explanations of collective decisions. Social psychology and civil-society study connect institutions to political behaviour. This broader programme responds to the confirmed compulsory political-science core; Dutch political specialization and final research training differ.

alternatives.concept: Study how political actors, groups and public arguments shape democracy and collective decisions. Comparative and international politics combine with social psychology, rhetoric, persuasion, media representation and negotiation. Qualitative and quantitative methods support evidence-based inquiry into participation, political behaviour and public debate. This focus gives less weight to legal and economic institutions than the first programme.

alternativeSelection.assessment: Two coherent evidence-backed and feasible programmes pass. A dedicated climate-politics third direction relies on an illustration/uninstantiated excluded choice, so stop without creating it.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Comparative parties, elections, regimes, institutions and theory-guided empirical inquiry directly address comparative politics and an important part of its research skills.
International-relations theories, comparative foreign-policy analysis and country-position research directly address international politics; integrated academic-skills structure differs.
EU institutions, integration, representation, legislation and empirical amendment research directly address the EU-politics substance; the external integrated academic-skills design differs.
Actual policy phases, national/international policy cases and memo writing address policy formation and implementation; the external integrated skills sequence is broader.
Public choice and model-based efficiency/equity analysis address an identifiable economic part of political decision-making; this is not the complete external economics and rational-choice course.
Political, economic and cultural transformations since 1815 directly address an important historical part; the external course starts in 1789 and has a more specifically European focus.
Constitutional institutions, rights, judicial review and administrative participation address core rule-of-law substance; Dutch constitutional history differs.
Original political texts, normative concept analysis and argument directly address political philosophy; different authors and scope are retained.
Social cognition, attitudes, influence, group processes and prejudice directly address identifiable psychological mechanisms; not the full political-psychology voting/elite curriculum.
Actual multivariate OLS/GLS/IV estimation and tests supply substantive quantitative-method correspondence. Stata/economic applications do not duplicate the external political-data/R design.

Operationalization, measurement, sampling, research designs and explicit empirical project address research-method fundamentals. Its statistical teaching also contributes but this row does not assert complete integrated equivalence.
Actual R data cleaning, description, visualisation and analysis directly address the introductory data-analysis function; hypothesis-testing breadth differs and is complemented elsewhere.
Qualitative design, interviews, documentary/visual evidence, coding and reflexive interpretation address substantive qualitative methodology.
Dutch political parties, coalition formation, institutional history and national practice have no dedicated selected UCR counterpart; broader comparative study is not a substitute.
Retained independently. Related theory or methods elsewhere do not justify a separate row match for this complete component.
UCR has real research-design, analysis and report projects, but generic shared research functions do not establish a separately supported component correspondence; preserve the blank.

audience.programmeDescription: In National and International Politics, students study power, institutions and public policy in the Netherlands, Europe and the wider world. They develop comparative, qualitative and quantitative research skills and complete a supervised thesis.
audience.comparisonExplanation: This comparison assesses Leiden’s confirmed 95 EC compulsory political-science core. UCR can combine sustained comparative and international politics with policy, political theory and empirical research, or give more weight to political behaviour and public communication. Dutch political specialization and the complete political-psychology sequence differ. The 25 EC restricted choices, 30 EC seminar and thesis, and full degree progression are excluded from the claim; 30 EC of genuine open study is shown separately.

curriculum.limitation: The published structure totals 180 EC. Only the 95 EC compulsory core is academically assessed here. The 25 EC restricted choices and the 30 EC seminar and thesis are retained as published categories but remain unassessed; detailed eligibility, offerings and final-work rules are unverified. The separate 30 EC open space has no assumed contents. A complete valid entrant pathway is not certified.

componentNotes.nip1-01: Studies Dutch elections, parties, coalition formation and relations between government and parliament.
componentNotes.nip1-03: Introduces political science approaches, including institutionalism, constructivism, feminism, Marxism, political psychology and normative theory.
componentNotes.nip1-06: Studies the democratic rule of law in the Netherlands, with comparisons to neighbouring countries and the United States.
componentNotes.nip1-09: Introduces statistical description, testing and data analysis using R.
componentNotes.y2-01: Builds on introductory statistics and develops multivariate analysis using political data and R.
componentNotes.y2-04: Connects economic models and rational choice to political behaviour and policy, including growth, inequality, trade and climate.
componentNotes.y2-05: Studies how emotions, prejudice, personality and group dynamics influence political behaviour.
componentNotes.y2-06: Forms part of the second-year research training: students analyse evidence and communicate findings in writing and presentations.
componentNotes.y2-07: Students develop their own political research proposal and practise giving constructive feedback.
componentNotes.y2-08: Choose five different 5 EC courses from: Democracy and Autocracy; States, Trade and Development; War, Peace and Security; Migration and Borders; Environment: Politics and Policy; Media and Political Communication; Politics of International Law; Philosophy of Freedom and Equality; Polarisation and Populism; The Netherlands in the World. The detailed course eligibility and offering rules for this route still need confirmation. This component is displayed as published but is outside this comparison’s assessed compulsory core.
componentNotes.y3-01: Thirty EC may be used for electives, a minor, study abroad or an internship. Selected courses require approval, with an exception for recognised 30 EC Leiden, Delft and Erasmus minors; sufficient level and no overlap with compulsory study are required. Honours courses and the Political Science, Mini-minor Political Science and Introduction Social Sciences minors cannot fill this space. Places and individual eligibility are not guaranteed.
componentNotes.y3-02: A specialist seminar uses current literature, discussion and research-led learning. Topics such as populism, security, climate policy and digital democracy are examples. Entry and assessment rules for this route still need confirmation. This component is displayed as published but is outside this comparison’s assessed compulsory core.
componentNotes.y3-03: Students formulate a question, design and conduct their own political science research, and write an individual thesis under supervision. A supervision plan is agreed with the first reader. Entry and assessment rules for this route still need confirmation. This component is displayed as published but is outside this comparison’s assessed compulsory core.

comparisonScope.label: Qualified academic-core comparison
comparisonScope.assessed: The ten first-year compulsory courses (60 EC) and seven named second-year compulsory courses (35 EC). All 180 published EC remain visible. The 30 EC genuine open-study allowance is shown separately, without assumed contents.
comparisonScope.excluded: The 25 EC restricted-choice package and 30 EC third-year seminar/thesis, together 55 EC, are outside the academic claim. Their applicable offerings, eligibility and final-work details, full degree comparability and cohort progression are not certified.

acceptance.claim: Two complete feasible UCR programmes meaningfully respond to the confirmed 95 EC NIP compulsory core through sustained political theory, comparative/international/EU politics, policy, qualitative and quantitative methods and concrete psychological and institutional study. The second gives substantially more weight to democratic publics and communication. Dutch political and political-psychology depth remain different. This is not a comparison of the restricted specialization, final research, full degree or graduation eligibility.
acceptance.targetContext: Leiden Political Science BSc, ordinary Dutch-taught National and International Politics route, September 2026 entrants. Neutral broad route; IRO and outgoing POL/IP requirements excluded. Core 95 EC; published 180 EC retained with genuine 30 open and unassessed 55 required/choice EC.
acceptance.challengeMethod: Separately identified same-AI source-first final pass reads underlying primary/current UCR evidence and exact finished inputs; no independent human or separate-agent review.

uncertainties.fact: Applicable later NIP course eligibility/offerings, five-of-ten restricted-choice combinations and seminar/thesis entry and assessment remain unverified.

adverseResolutions.resolution: Restricted choices and final research impose intensive specialized domestic, security, communication or psychological training.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: This could alter whole-degree comparability and is not called immaterial. The 55 EC restricted/final-work scope is explicitly unassessed; it cannot erase the independently specified compulsory 95 EC political and methodological core. No final-work match or elective package is certified.

adverseResolutions.resolution: Future adopted rules change entry sequencing, assessment or available choices.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: No full valid pathway or eligibility is claimed. The current compulsory core and actual UCR teaching remain the evidence for the narrow academic judgment. Reassess a future complete-degree comparison when those rules are available; do not borrow outgoing POL/IP or IRO conditions.

uncertainties.fact: Open-study individual permission, nonoverlap, sufficient level and placement availability remain conditional.

adverseResolutions.resolution: A selected minor, exchange or internship is unavailable or refused.
adverseResolutions.effectOnClaim: No such selection is instantiated or used to support the academic match. The actual 30 EC category and its conditions are preserved separately; the 95 EC compulsory-core judgment does not depend on particular open contents.
